title: engine-loop decision — one judgement point
description: The highest-value record: a question, the episodes that bear on it, the reasoning that connects them, the answer, and — most importantly — what the answer rules out. A decision is what turns a pile of measurements into a policy. `judgement` is the gate that stops a refuted hypothesis from being trained on as a positive example.

question.description: The question must be falsifiable as written. 'Is the GPU slow?' is not; 'Is the ~44% of step time removable serialization, or is the GPU genuinely busy?' is.

artifact.description: repo-relative path when the evidence is a document rather than a run

reading.description: What the evidence SAYS — the numbers, not a restatement of the episode's goal.

reasoning.description: The inference from evidence to conclusion, including which of the readings are load-bearing and which are structural artifacts. A conclusion with no reasoning is an opinion.

judgement.description: sound = still believed; refuted = later evidence contradicted it (then superseded_by MUST be set); unresolved = the evidence did not settle it. This field is the anti-training-poison gate: refuted decisions never become positive examples.

action.description: What was actually done as a result. This is the supervised target for the (state -> next move) projection.

ruled_out.description: Hypotheses this decision kills, with the evidence that killed them. Negative knowledge is what stops a later agent from re-walking the same path; it is the single most reused thing in this loop.

superseded_by.description: decision_id that replaced this one. Must resolve. Required non-null when judgement == 'refuted'.
